item.title: Iran War Live Updates: U.S. and Iran Sign Preliminary Deal, but Its Terms Remain Secret
item.description: President Trump and Iran’s lead negotiator have signed an agreement that was expected to open the Strait of Hormuz. But the specific terms of the deal have not been released, and Israel’s leader appears not to be fully on board.

item.title: Israelis denounce Trump’s deal with Iran
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu did not issue an immediate statement, but other Israelis disparaged the peace deal and said Israel’s fight against Hezbollah in Lebanon would go on.

item.title: Middle East live: Trump says Iran deal has been signed, text to be released after Friday ceremony
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Monday said a memorandum of understanding with Iran has already been signed and that the text of the deal would be released sometime ​after ‌a formal signing ceremony on Friday, adding ⁠that the Strait of Hormuz would also be fully open by then. The US leader said he did not know if he would attend the Friday ​ceremony expected in Geneva, but that Vice President JD Vance would attend. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

item.title: Iran war 'has been a strategic disaster for the State of Israel', analyst says
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is on a collision course with Donald Trump as the U.S. president seeks to extricate himself from the war, with both men's goals unmet and Israeli military operations tied down in Lebanon. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Aaron David Miller, Senior Fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, says that "this has been a strategic disaster for the state of Israel. item.title: U.S. and Iran Sign a Framework Deal, Leaving Major Issues for Future Talks
item.description: U.S. and Iranian officials said the deal included a 60-day cease-fire to pave the way for negotiations toward a final peace agreement and talks on Iran’s nuclear program.

item.title: Iran deal: Trump is back to square one, but the cards are now in Tehran’s favor
item.description: The signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the US and Iran on Monday has been welcomed by the international community after a devastating three-month war. The agreement was announced on June 14, President Donald Trump’s birthday, but the biggest beneficiary, experts say, is the Iranian regime.

item.title: Interim US-Iran peace deal sparks anger among Israelis, who lash out at Netanyahu
item.description: Israelis from across the political spectrum reacted angrily Monday to the news of an initial deal between the U.S. and Iran, calling it a disaster for Israel and directing their fury at one man: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

item.title: Israel to stay ‘indefinitely’ in lands seized in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria
item.description: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said on Monday that Israeli ground forces would remain in land they hold in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, potentially challenging a memorandum of understanding announced a day earlier between the US and Iran to end the war in the Middle East.

item.title: U.S. and Iran announce an initial deal to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: The deal is a major breakthrough in the conflict that set the Middle East aflame and shook the global economy. However, it did not resolve critical issues set aside for further negotiations.

item.title: Iran deal presents political nightmare for Netanyahu
item.description: Donald Trump's ceasefire agreement with Iran leaves the Israeli PM trapped in a new political and security dilemma.
